thread:
maria.g: Quick check — trying to use the Node/TS SDK in a Next.js Edge route. Getting ESM import errors when bundling and intermittent auth header missing on retries while streaming. Anyone seen this?

alex.h: Yup, saw similar. Error message?

maria.g: Build-time error: 'Must use import to load ES Module' when serverless/edge bundle tries to require the SDK. At runtime streaming requests sometimes come back 401 on the second chunk after a retry.

jonathan.k: For Next Edge you need the SDK to be ESM-compatible at bundle time. Are you using `require()` anywhere?

maria.g: No, import style: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` — but rollup/vite/next bundler transforms cause it to inject `require` into the edge build apparently.

liam.s: Two things: 1) bundlers (Vite/Next) often need explicit SSR/noExternal or optimizeDeps includes. 2) retries + streaming: if the SDK replays the request without re-attaching the auth header (or if credential resolution relies on process.env in a worker), you can see 401s.

nidhi: For Vercel/Next Edge we recommend shipping an ESM-only build and marking the package as "sideEffects": false and adding proper exports. On the app side, try adding in next.config.js: 

```js
// next.config.js
module.exports = {
  experimental: { esmExternals: "loose" },
  webpack: (config, { isServer }) => {
    if (!isServer) {
      config.resolve.fallback = { fs: false };
    }
    return config;
  },
};
```

liam.s: For Vite dev builds, do `optimizeDeps.include: ['@redwood/inference']` and `ssr.noExternal: ['@redwood/inference']` so it doesn't transform ESM to CJS at build-time.

alex.h: Also check package.json exports. We moved the SDK to provide a `browser` and an `edge` ESM entry. If your build pulls the CJS entry, you'll hit the import/require mismatch.

maria.g: Good call. How about the auth/header replay issue?

jonathan.k: Streaming + retry behavior: when a transient network error occurs we re-issue the request. In Node we re-read the stream, but in Edge/Web Streams you can only read once unless we clone the body. If the SDK retries without cloning the body and re-attaching headers (or if the API key is read from process.env which isn't available in Edge runtime), you'll get 401.

nidhi: Recommended pattern for Next Edge: keep secrets server-side (Server Functions / Middleware). Don't expose them to the Edge runtime. If you must call from Edge, pass an ephemeral token from a server route or use signed cookies.

maria.g: Is there a quick workaround for local dev while using Edge routes?

liam.s: For local dev, set NEXT_RUNTIME=edge and add `NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_PROXY` to point to a local server that injects the API key. Ugly but fast for iteration. Otherwise keep calls server-side.

alex.h: On the SDK side, we can add a guard: detect Web Stream body and clone for retry (via `tee()` on ReadableStream) and ensure we reapply headers from the original request options. I filed a tiny task for this.

maria.g: Can you drop the PR? I can test it against our app.

alex.h: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 — adds `streamCloneForRetry` util and updates retry logic to preserve headers. Also exposes an ESM-only entry `dist/edge/index.mjs`.

jonathan.k: Nice. For Next users we should update the README with recommended next.config/vite config and an Edge caveats section.

devex-bot: Reminder: update SDK docs for edge runtime support — label docs-needed.

maria.g: Thanks — pinging @alex.h for review on a small change in our app that changes how we import the SDK (swapping require -> import). Alex, can you review #1023?

alex.h: On it. I'll try to get to it today — pinging @nidhi for any platform config notes.

nidhi: Will add a short snippet to the deploy checklist (Vercel envs + middleware recommendation).

deploy-bot: Deployed preview for PR #412 at https://deploy-preview-412.vercel.app — includes edge entry + tests.

maria.g: I tested the preview — bundle no longer fails and streaming retry behavior looks stable (no 401s on forced network flaps). Thanks! :tada:

liam.s: Follow-up: we should add a small test harness that simulates stream interruptions in CI to prevent regressions.

jonathan.k: Agreed. I'll add a flaky-stream simulation to the SDK integration tests.

maria.g: Awesome. TL;DR for anyone skimming: 1) ensure your bundler doesn't transpile ESM to CJS (use next/vite config), 2) don't expose API keys to public edge code, prefer server-side or ephemeral tokens, 3) SDK PR adds stream clone + preserves headers for retries.

alex.h: Thanks for testing everyone — will merge once CI and docs updated.

maria.g: Thanks all. Closing the loop.
